intro.title: Build timeout and cancellation for HTTP clients
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple HTTP client in Node.js that can set a timeout to automatically cancel requests that take too long. You'll learn how to use the built-in `fetch` API along with the `AbortController` and `AbortSignal` to implement request cancellation. This will help you manage network reliability by preventing your application from hanging indefinitely on slow or unresponsive servers. By the end, you'll have a practical understanding of handling timeouts and graceful error handling in HTTP communications.
intro.usecase: Timeout and cancellation for HTTP clients is essential in any production Node.js application that communicates with external services. In e-commerce platforms, this prevents checkout processes from hanging indefinitely when payment gateways are slow. API dashboards use timeouts to ensure slow third-party data providers don't freeze the entire interface. Search autocomplete features implement cancellation to discard outdated requests as users type, while file upload services need timeouts to handle network interruptions gracefully.
